title: Food & Meals (食物与三餐)
description: Talk about breakfast, lunch and dinner, name common Chinese foods and drinks, use 吃 and 喝 correctly, say what you like and want, order a meal, and learn basic Chinese table manners.

notes.heading: 🍽️ The Three Meals (三餐 sān cān)
notes.body:
Chinese meal words build from time words + 饭 **fàn** (cooked rice / meal):

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 早饭 | zǎofàn | breakfast |
| 午饭 | wǔfàn | lunch |
| 晚饭 | wǎnfàn | dinner |
| 吃饭 | chīfàn | to eat a meal |

💡 **Worked Example:** 你吃早饭了吗？Nǐ chī zǎofàn le ma? — Have you eaten breakfast? In China, asking 吃了吗？(Have you eaten?) is a warm, everyday greeting.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 早 **zǎo** = morning, 午 **wǔ** = noon, 晚 **wǎn** = evening — you met these in greetings (早上好, 晚上好).
- 饭 **fàn** alone means cooked rice, but inside these words it means 'meal'.
- A common question: 你想吃什么？Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme? — What do you want to eat?

notes.heading: 🍚 Common Chinese Foods
notes.body:
| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 米饭 | mǐfàn | (cooked) rice |
| 面条 | miàntiáo | noodles |
| 饺子 | jiǎozi | dumplings |
| 包子 | bāozi | steamed stuffed buns |
| 鸡蛋 | jīdàn | egg |
| 面包 | miànbāo | bread |
| 水果 | shuǐguǒ | fruit |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我们晚上吃饺子。Wǒmen wǎnshang chī jiǎozi. — We eat dumplings in the evening.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 饺子 are traditional at Chinese New Year — their shape resembles old silver ingots, symbolising wealth.
- 面 **miàn** means wheat/noodles; 米 **mǐ** means rice (uncooked). Northern China favours wheat foods, the south favours rice.
- Counting food: 一碗米饭 (a bowl of rice, 碗 wǎn = bowl), 一个包子 (one baozi).

notes.heading: 🥤 Drinks (饮料 yǐnliào)
notes.body:
| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 水 | shuǐ | water |
| 茶 | chá | tea |
| 牛奶 | niúnǎi | milk |
| 果汁 | guǒzhī | fruit juice |
| 咖啡 | kāfēi | coffee |
| 可乐 | kělè | cola |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我想喝一杯茶。Wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi chá. — I'd like to drink a cup of tea. (杯 **bēi** = cup/glass, the measure word for drinks)

📎 **Key Points:**
- 茶 chá is hugely important in China — guests are traditionally welcomed with hot tea.
- 牛 **niú** = cow, so 牛奶 is literally 'cow milk'.
- 果 **guǒ** = fruit, 汁 **zhī** = juice, so 果汁 = fruit juice.
- 热 **rè** = hot, 冰 **bīng** = iced: 热茶 (hot tea), 冰水 (iced water).

notes.heading: 🍴 Two Verbs: 吃 (eat) and 喝 (drink)
notes.body:
- **吃 chī** = to eat — for solid food: 吃饭, 吃面条, 吃饺子
- **喝 hē** = to drink — for liquids: 喝水, 喝茶, 喝牛奶

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 我吃米饭。Wǒ chī mǐfàn. — I eat rice.
- 他喝茶。Tā hē chá. — He drinks tea.
- 你吃什么？Nǐ chī shénme? — What are you eating?

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** English 'have' covers both, but Chinese needs the right verb — never 喝米饭 (drink rice) or 吃水 (eat water).

🔑 **How it works:** interesting exception — 吃药 **chī yào** (take medicine) uses 吃 even though you swallow it with water, and 喝酒 **hē jiǔ** (drink alcohol) uses 喝 as expected.

notes.heading: ❤️ Likes, Dislikes & Wants
notes.body:
Talk about food preferences with these verbs:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 喜欢 | xǐhuan | to like |
| 爱 | ài | to love |
| 想 | xiǎng | to want / would like |
| 要 | yào | to want (stronger) |

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 我喜欢吃饺子。Wǒ xǐhuan chī jiǎozi. — I like eating dumplings.
- 我不爱喝咖啡。Wǒ bú ài hē kāfēi. — I don't love drinking coffee.
- 你想吃什么？Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme? — What would you like to eat?

🔑 **How it works:** these verbs can be followed directly by another verb: 喜欢吃 (like eating), 想喝 (want to drink). Negatives use 不: 不喜欢, 不想.

📎 **Key Point:** 想 is softer and more polite than 要 — like 'would like' vs 'want' in English.

notes.heading: 🧾 Ordering Basics: 我要…
notes.body:
Ordering in a restaurant is easy with 我要 **wǒ yào** (I'll have / I want):

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 服务员 | fúwùyuán | waiter / waitress |
| 我要… | wǒ yào … | I'll have … |
| 请给我… | qǐng gěi wǒ … | please give me … |
| 还要别的吗？ | hái yào biéde ma? | anything else? |
| 多少钱？ | duōshao qián? | how much is it? |
| 买单！ | mǎidān! | the bill, please! |

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 服务员！我要一碗米饭和一杯茶。Fúwùyuán! Wǒ yào yì wǎn mǐfàn hé yì bēi chá. — Waiter! I'll have a bowl of rice and a cup of tea.
B: 还要别的吗？Hái yào biéde ma? — Anything else?
A: 不要了，谢谢。Bú yào le, xièxie. — No thanks.

📎 **Key Point:** 和 **hé** means 'and' when joining two things: 米饭和茶 (rice and tea).

notes.heading: 🥢 Chopsticks & Table Culture
notes.body:
Chopsticks are 筷子 **kuàizi** — used in pairs (一双筷子).

**Table culture basics:**

- Food is usually **shared**: dishes sit in the middle and everyone takes a little.
- It is polite to let older people or guests start eating first.
- 请 **qǐng** (please) and 慢用 **màn yòng** (enjoy your meal, literally 'use slowly') are common table phrases.

⚠️ **Chopstick don'ts:**
- Never stick chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice — it resembles incense at a funeral.
- Don't point at people with your chopsticks.
- Don't dig through a shared dish hunting for the best piece.

💡 **Worked Example:** 你会用筷子吗？Nǐ huì yòng kuàizi ma? — Can you use chopsticks? (会 **huì** = can/know how to; 用 **yòng** = to use)

✅ **Check:** 我用筷子吃面条。Wǒ yòng kuàizi chī miàntiáo. — I eat noodles with chopsticks.

flashcards.definition: Breakfast. 早 = morning, 饭 = meal.
flashcards.example: 我七点吃早饭。Wǒ qī diǎn chī zǎofàn. (I eat breakfast at seven.)

flashcards.term: 午饭 wǔfàn / 晚饭 wǎnfàn
flashcards.definition: Lunch / dinner. 午 = noon, 晚 = evening.
flashcards.example: 我们十二点吃午饭。Wǒmen shí'èr diǎn chī wǔfàn. (We eat lunch at twelve.)

flashcards.definition: Cooked rice. Measure word: 碗 (一碗米饭 = a bowl of rice).
flashcards.example: 我要一碗米饭。Wǒ yào yì wǎn mǐfàn. (I'll have a bowl of rice.)
我喜欢吃面条。Wǒ xǐhuan chī miàntiáo. (I like eating noodles.)

flashcards.definition: Dumplings — traditional at Chinese New Year.
flashcards.example: 我们晚上吃饺子。Wǒmen wǎnshang chī jiǎozi. (We eat dumplings in the evening.)
爷爷爱喝茶。Yéye ài hē chá. (Grandpa loves drinking tea.)
我早上喝牛奶。Wǒ zǎoshang hē niúnǎi. (I drink milk in the morning.)

flashcards.definition: To eat — for solid food (吃饭, 吃面条).
flashcards.example: 你想吃什么？Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme? (What would you like to eat?)

flashcards.definition: To drink — for liquids (喝水, 喝茶).
flashcards.example: 我想喝一杯果汁。Wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi guǒzhī. (I'd like a glass of juice.)

flashcards.definition: To like / to love — can be followed by another verb: 喜欢吃 (like eating).
flashcards.example: 我很喜欢吃饺子。Wǒ hěn xǐhuan chī jiǎozi. (I really like eating dumplings.)

flashcards.definition: I'll have … / I want … — the key phrase for ordering.
flashcards.example: 我要一杯茶。Wǒ yào yì bēi chá. (I'll have a cup of tea.)

flashcards.definition: Chopsticks — used in pairs (一双筷子).
flashcards.example: 我用筷子吃饭。Wǒ yòng kuàizi chīfàn. (I eat with chopsticks.)

questions.explanation: 早 means morning and 饭 means meal, so 早饭 is breakfast. Lunch is 午饭 and dinner is 晚饭.
饺子 jiǎozi are dumplings, traditionally eaten at Chinese New Year because their shape recalls old silver ingots.
喝 hē means to drink — used with liquids like 水 (water), 茶 (tea) and 牛奶 (milk). Eating uses 吃.
牛奶 literally means 'cow milk' — 牛 (cow) + 奶 (milk). Tea is 茶 and juice is 果汁.
筷子 kuàizi are chopsticks, used in pairs (一双筷子) for eating most Chinese food.

questions.stem: Which verb is correct: 我想___一杯茶。(I'd like to drink a cup of tea.)
questions.explanation: Tea is a liquid, so it takes the verb 喝 (to drink): 喝一杯茶. 吃 is only for solid food.

questions.stem: 我喜欢吃饺子。(Wǒ xǐhuan chī jiǎozi.) means:
questions.explanation: 喜欢 (like) can be followed directly by another verb, so 喜欢吃饺子 is 'like eating dumplings'. Wanting would use 想 or 要.

questions.stem: In a restaurant, how do you say 'I'll have a bowl of rice'?
choices: 我要一碗米饭。Wǒ yào yì wǎn mǐfàn.
我吃一碗米饭。Wǒ chī yì wǎn mǐfàn.
你喜欢米饭吗？Nǐ xǐhuan mǐfàn ma?
questions.explanation: 我要… (I'll have…) is the ordering phrase, and 碗 is the measure word for a bowl: 我要一碗米饭.

questions.stem: 你吃了吗？(Nǐ chī le ma?) is often used in China as:
choices: A way to complain about food
A way to order a meal
questions.explanation: 吃了吗？(Have you eaten?) is a traditional friendly greeting, showing care — much like 'how are you?' in English.

questions.stem: 还要别的吗？(Hái yào biéde ma?) is something a waiter asks to mean:
questions.explanation: 还 (also/still) + 要 (want) + 别的 (other things) + 吗 = 'do you also want other things?' — the standard 'anything else?'

questions.stem: Which is considered BAD table manners in China?
choices: Letting older people start eating first
Sharing dishes placed in the middle of the table
Sticking chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice
questions.explanation: Chopsticks stuck upright in rice look like incense burned at funerals, so it is a serious table taboo. The other options are all polite customs.
Milk is a liquid, so 喝牛奶 (drink milk) is correct. Rice and dumplings are solid food needing 吃, and tea is a liquid needing 喝.

questions.stem: 小明 says 我不爱喝咖啡。(Wǒ bú ài hē kāfēi.) What does he mean?
choices: He doesn't like drinking coffee much.
questions.explanation: 不 negates 爱 (love), so 不爱喝咖啡 = doesn't love drinking coffee — a dislike statement, not a statement about ability or buying.

questions.stem: A friend asks 你想吃什么？(Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme?) Which is a correct reply?
choices: 我想吃面条。Wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáo.
面条很好吃在。Miàntiáo hěn hǎochī zài.
questions.explanation: The question uses 想吃 (would like to eat), so the natural reply mirrors it: 我想吃面条 (I'd like to eat noodles). Noodles are solid, so 喝 is wrong.

questions.stem: Listen to this dialogue: A: 服务员！我要一碗米饭和一杯茶。B: 还要别的吗？A: 不要了，多少钱？What is A doing at the end?
questions.explanation: 多少钱？means 'how much money?' — after ordering rice and tea and refusing extras, A is asking for the price, i.e. asking to pay.
